references.text: The foreigner living among you shall follow the same law as the native-born.
Moses reminds the people of the day they stood before the Lord at Horeb to hear his words and learn to fear him.
The purpose of the commandments is that Israel should fear the Lord and keep his statutes.
Context for the assembly: the law shall be read aloud when all Israel comes to appear before the Lord.
Joshua reads the entire law to the assembly, including women, children, and foreigners, in accordance with Moses' command.
Ezra gathers all the people, men, women, and all who could understand, to hear the law being read.
An invitation to come and listen in order to learn reverence for God.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge and wisdom.
Paul speaks to Israelites and God-fearing people in the synagogue, which included both Jews and proselytes.
The holy Scriptures are able to make one wise for salvation and are useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness.
